newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's SES to become more regional - Hu.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's SES to become more regional - Hu.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) gives investors a regional exposure to Asian economies and this is set to grow, Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Friday.

"Investors in the stock market here do not merely end up with exposure to Singapore...they gain regional exposure. And this regional component in our stock market is set to increase in importance," Hu said.
Hu was addressing the annual meeting of the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) being held in Singapore.

"Already the profits of a number of companies listed on the SES do not depend on the state of the domestic Singapore economy, simply because they do not derive any significant proportion of their revenues from Singapore," he said.
Hu noted Singapore had embarked on a course to attract companies with operations in the region to raise funds from the Singapore market.
He said there were 45 such regional companies listed on the SES, comprising 24 percent of total market capitalisation.
Singapore's domestic companies would also have to look to expand regionally. "Going regional is the only way to break free of the confines of a small domestic market," Hu said.
"If the current trend continues, by the turn of the century, an investor who buys into companies listed on the SES will effectively be investing in the economic futures of the region," Hu added.
